title: Custom Bridge Networks & DNS Magic 🪄
description: Create isolated networks and let containers discover each other by name.

slides.title: Creating a Custom Bridge Network 🛠️
slides.content:
# `docker network create`

```bash
docker network create --driver bridge my-net
```

- `--driver bridge` is the default; you can omit it.
- You can also specify `--subnet`, `--gateway`, `--ip-range`, etc.

**Example:**
```bash
docker network create --subnet=10.0.0.0/24 my-app-net
```

This creates an isolated virtual network separate from the default bridge.

slides.title: DNS – Service Discovery by Name 🏷️
slides.content:
# Automatic Name Resolution

On a custom bridge network, Docker embeds a DNS server (at `127.0.0.11`) that resolves container **names** to their IP addresses.

- Start containers on the same network using `--network`.
- Assign them names (`--name`).
- Now they can ping each other by **name**!

```bash
docker run -d --name web --network my-net nginx
docker run -d --name db --network my-net postgres
docker exec web ping -c 2 db
```

> No more hardcoding IPs! This is a game‑changer for microservices.

quizData.question: What makes custom bridge networks superior to the default bridge for container‑to‑container communication?

options.text: They provide automatic DNS resolution by container name
They allow containers to share the host network

quizData.explanation: Custom bridge networks include a built‑in DNS server, so containers can find each other by name.

slides.title: Full DNS Demo 🧪
slides.content: Create a network and two containers that talk by name:
slides.codeSnippet:
# Create network
docker network create demo-net

# Start a web server and a database container
docker run -d --name web --network demo-net nginx:alpine
docker run -d --name db --network demo-net alpine sleep 3600

# Ping db from web by name
docker exec web ping -c 2 db

# Also works from db to web
docker exec db ping -c 2 web

slides.title: Network Isolation 🧱
slides.content:
# Separate Stacks, Separate Networks

Containers on different custom networks **cannot** communicate directly (unless you connect them).

This provides built‑in segmentation for security and clarity.

Example:
- `front-tier` network for web and API.
- `back-tier` network for API and database.

Place the API container on both networks to bridge them.

quizData.question: A container on `net1` can ping a container on `net2` by name without extra configuration.
quizData.explanation: By default, different Docker networks are isolated. You need to connect a container to both networks to route traffic.
